caption_used: Двупанелна линейна графика, илюстрираща средните леглодни (А) и структурния ефект върху тях (Б) за периода 2008–2021 г. Фигура А показва, че средните леглодни намаляват от около 278 дни през 2008 г. до приблизително 195 дни през 2021 г., като най-рязък спад се наблюдава между 2013 и 2017 г. Фигура Б разкрива, че структурният ефект варира между 0,5% и 2,8%, с минимум от около 0,3% през 2012 г., след което нараства плавно и равномерно до 2,8% през 2021 г.
raw_response:
The figure is a two-panel line graph illustrating changes in average bed days and the structural effect on them over the period 2008-2021. Both panels share the same x-axis, labeled "Години" (Years), with a categorical scale showing the years 2008, 2012/2013, 2017, and 2021, with equal spacing between the labels.

The left panel (A) has a y-axis labeled "Средни леглодни (дни)" (Average bed days), with a linear scale ranging from 200 to 280 days, marked at intervals of 20 days. The red line graph starts at approximately 278 days in 2008, decreases slightly to around 265 days in 2012/2013, followed by a sharp drop to about 240 days in 2017, and finally decreases to roughly 195 days in 2021.

The right panel (B) has a y-axis labeled "Структурен ефект върху средни леглодни (%)" (Structural effect on average bed days (%)), with a linear scale ranging from 1.0% to 2.0%, marked at intervals of 0.5%. The red line graph begins at around 1.5% in 2008, drops to approximately 0.3% in 2012/2013, then rises to about 1.2% in 2017, and finally surges to roughly 2.8% in 2021.

DESCRIPTION: The figure is a two-panel line graph showing the average bed days (Panel A) and the structural effect on average bed days (Panel B) over the years 2008, 2012/2013, 2017, and 2021. In Panel A, the average bed days decrease from approximately 278 days in 2008 to around 195 days in 2021. In Panel B, the structural effect varies, starting at around 1.5% in 2008, dropping to about 0.3% in 2012/2013, increasing to roughly 1.2% in 2017, and reaching approximately 2.8% in 2021.
